# E0334: member type that names nothing

A member type such as `C.Item` names a parameter of a trait that bounds `C`. Check the name against the trait's parameters.

- Rule: [`traits.member-types`](../../reference/11-traits.md#traits.member-types)
- Reported at: the member type.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0334:5
trait Collection<Item> {
  fn at(self, i: i64) -> Option<Item>
}

fn first<C: Collection>(c: C) -> Option<C.Key> { None }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
trait Collection<Item> {
  fn at(self, i: i64) -> Option<Item>
}

fn first<C: Collection>(c: C) -> Option<C.Item> { c.at(0) }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0334_member_type_that_names_nothing.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0334_member_type_that_names_nothing.lt):

```text
── MEMBER TYPE THAT NAMES NOTHING ── E0334_member_type_that_names_nothing.lt:5:41  [E0334]

No bound of `C` has a parameter `Key`:

  5 │ fn first<C: Collection>(c: C) -> Option<C.Key> { None }
    │                                         ^^^^^

A member type such as `C.Item` names a parameter of a trait that bounds `C`.
Check the name against the trait's parameters.
```
